what: Resolution gate: every structural element present in an OFFICIAL NPHIES sample must be KNOWN to the compiled spec in src/spec/. Unresolved identifiers mean the compiled spec is incomplete, not that the sample is wrong.

method.elementsFound: distinct structural identifiers per sample (segments, populated fields, templateIds, sections, bundle entry resourceTypes, profile URLs, SOAP element paths, XDS metadata attribute names)
method.elementsResolved: exact matches + matches that required normalising a mangled spec literal
method.normalisedMatch: the identifier exists in the compiled spec but only after stripping injected whitespace, trailing footnote digits or case differences — counted as resolved, reported as an extraction defect
method.structuralMismatch: the element resolves but contradicts a compiled rule (order, usage X/NP, fixed value, bundle type, entry list membership)
method.notMeasured: value-level conformance (code systems, value sets, datatypes, lengths) is out of scope for this gate
method.scope: `overall` and `byFormat` count ONLY baseline-scope elements — the same identifiers the previous run counted — so the figures are directly comparable. Checks added by this pass are scope "extended" and are counted in `overallExtended` and `byElementKindExtended`.
method.independence: Every resolved identifier is tagged with the PROVENANCE of the compiled rule that resolved it. A rule derived from a golden sample cannot confirm that same sample; see the `independence` section.

independence.headline: SOAP/XDS resolves 100.0% overall, but only 55.0% against rules that did NOT come from these same samples. The second number is the honest one.

provenanceMeaning.confluence: INDEPENDENT — a cached Confluence page states it
provenanceMeaning.confluence+sample: INDEPENDENT — a Confluence row, confirmed against a sample
provenanceMeaning.standard: INDEPENDENT of the samples — published IHE/ebRIM/HL7 constant, but NOT NPHIES-confirmed
provenanceMeaning.sample: CIRCULAR — the rule was read off a golden sample, so resolving that sample proves nothing
provenanceMeaning.prose-mention: WEAKEST — the literal appears only inside narrative text in the bundle, never as a locator or fixed value
provenanceMeaning.unattributed: the compiled member carries no provenance at all — treat as unverified

overallExtended.note: baseline identifiers PLUS the checks this pass added (ebRIM content model, CDA header order, FHIR two-family rule). Not comparable with the previous run — compare `overall` for that.

coverageExtensions.what: @objectType, @classificationNode, @status, @associationType, the rim:Name of every Classification/ExternalIdentifier, rim:Description, referential integrity of classifiedObject/registryObject/sourceObject/targetObject, ebRIM child sequence, and the ITI-41 Document@id ↔ ExtrinsicObject@id binding
coverageExtensions.wasPreviouslyBlind: the baseline gate saw only element PATHS and Slot names; none of the ebRIM identity attributes were checked

coverageExtensions.what: the sample's header children are checked against the ORDERED member list of the compiled "ClinicalDocument header (document order)" group, and any header element the compiled sequence does not place is reported as unsequenced
coverageExtensions.wasPreviouslyBlind: the baseline gate only asked whether each header element NAME was known somewhere in the spec

coverageExtensions.check: two-family rule (Bundle.type + first entry) per sample
coverageExtensions.what: document family = Bundle.type "document" opening with a Composition; message family = Bundle.type "message" opening with a MessageHeader. Checked as one fact per sample, including whether the COMPILED pair is itself self-consistent
coverageExtensions.wasPreviouslyBlind: the baseline gate raised two independent mismatches and silently checked nothing when the compiled structure lacked either rule

coverageExtensions.check: internal consistency of structures with no golden sample
coverageExtensions.what: reported in `unverifiedStructures`; deliberately NOT counted as resolution — internally consistent is not verified
coverageExtensions.wasPreviouslyBlind: saml-sso was invisible to the gate entirely

unverifiedStructures.confidenceReason: The element tree, its order, its attribute names and every fixed urn value come from one LITERAL XML skeleton published by NPHIES, so those facts are individually high-confidence. The structure as a whole is "medium" because (a) no official sample exists to check it against, (b) the skeleton is published without its signature and the signature's shape is unspecified, (c) the SSO flow around the message lives in two unreadable diagram images, and (d) one binding — Provider ID to saml:NameID — rests on a colour highlight rather than a sentence.
